thesis: Consciousness requires distinguishing functional access, report, selfhood and felt experience, while preserving testable disagreement.
role: Surveys theories and ethical costs without declaring a winner.

ideas.statement: Report is neither a sufficient nor necessary standalone certificate of experience.
Predefined adversarial predictions turn philosophical disagreement into selective evidence without settling whole metaphysical systems.
Artificial origin and fluent speech do not settle sentience; decisions must address uncertain and asymmetric harms.
Competing metaphysics each owe an account of unity, dependence or explanatory gaps.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: COGITATE supported and challenged aspects of both tested theory families.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Functional coordination tests do not alone identify experience; indicators depend on theories and architecture.

audit.notes: Every unit read; metaphysical commitments separated from empirical findings.
